title: Interview practice: Neighbourhoods and learning new skills
author: toefl-claude-test-generator
description: Two speaking interviews: local neighbourhoods and community life; learning new skills outside school.

tasks.intro: Hi, thanks for joining me today. I'm researching how people feel about the places they live, so I'd like to ask you a few questions about your neighbourhood.

questions.text: To begin, could you describe the neighbourhood where you live now? What do you like most about it?
Tell me about a local place, like a shop, park or café, that you visit often. Why do you keep going back there?
Some people prefer living in a busy city centre, while others prefer a quiet residential area. Which would you choose, and how do the two compare for someone your age?
Many people today don't know their neighbours at all. Do you think it's still important for communities to be close? Why or why not?

tasks.intro: Hello, and welcome. Today I'm talking with people about how they learn new skills outside the classroom.

questions.text: First, can you tell me about a skill you've learned outside of school, such as cooking, a sport or a musical instrument? How did you learn it?
What was the most difficult part of learning that skill, and what did you do to get past it?
Some people learn best by taking lessons with a teacher, while others prefer teaching themselves. Which approach works better for you, and why?
Some people believe employers should pay for their workers to learn new skills, even ones not directly related to the job. Do you agree? Please explain your view.
